sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Tricep Cable Extension is an isolation exercise that targets the triceps using a cable machine with a rope attachment.

This movement effectively isolates all three heads of the triceps through a full range of motion, making it one of the most popular arm exercises in the gym.

The cable provides constant tension throughout the movement, which is superior to free weights for maintaining muscle engagement at every point of the rep.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Constant tension on the triceps throughout the entire range of motion
- Effectively targets all three heads of the triceps
- Easy to adjust weight for drop sets and progressive overload
- Low risk of injury when performed with proper form
- Great for building arm size and definition
- Improves lockout strength for pressing movements
- Suitable for all fitness levels

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Triceps (Long Head, Lateral Head, Medial Head)

Secondary: Forearms, Core (stabilization)

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Stand facing the cable machine with a rope attachment connected to the high pulley.
2. Grasp each end of the rope with an overhand grip.
3. Bring your hands to the sides of your head with your elbows bent.
4. Keep your feet shoulder-width apart with a slight bend in the knees.
5. Stand upright with your core engaged and chest up.
6. Tuck your elbows close to your sides.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Keeping your upper arms stationary, slowly extend your arms downward.
2. Contract your triceps as you push the rope toward the floor.
3. At the bottom of the movement, spread the rope ends apart slightly for a full contraction.
4. Pause briefly at the bottom, squeezing your triceps.
5. Slowly return your hands back to the starting position with control.
6. Repeat the movement for the desired number of reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Flaring the elbows out to the sides during the movement
- Using momentum or swinging the body to push the weight down
- Leaning too far forward over the cable
- Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
- Moving the upper arms instead of keeping them stationary
- Using too much weight and sacrificing form
- Rushing through reps without controlling the eccentric phase

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Cable Machine with High Pulley
- Rope Attachment (most common)
- Alternative: Straight Bar or V-Bar Attachment
- Appropriate Weight Selection

sections.heading: Cable Machine Setup
sections.content:
1. Set the pulley to the highest position on the cable machine.
2. Attach a rope handle to the cable clip.
3. Select an appropriate weight — start lighter to master form.
4. Ensure the cable runs smoothly without any obstructions.
5. Stand close enough to the machine that the cable stays taut.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Feet: Shoulder-width apart, one foot slightly forward for stability.
2. Knees: Slightly bent, not locked out.
3. Torso: Upright with a slight forward lean from the hips.
4. Elbows: Tucked close to your sides, pointing straight down.
5. Grip: Overhand grip on each end of the rope.
6. Core: Engaged throughout to prevent swaying.
7. Shoulders: Down and back, away from the ears.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Overhead Tricep Extension: Cable or dumbbell variation targeting the long head
- Skull Crushers: Barbell or dumbbell lying tricep extension
- Close Grip Bench Press: Compound pressing with tricep emphasis
- Dips: Bodyweight tricep-dominant pressing movement
- Kickbacks: Dumbbell isolation for the triceps
- Diamond Push-Ups: Bodyweight tricep-focused push-up variation

sections.heading: Cable Extension Variations
sections.content:
Rope Pushdown: Standard tricep cable extension with rope
Straight Bar Pushdown: Using a straight bar for a different grip angle
V-Bar Pushdown: Using a V-bar attachment for neutral grip
Single Arm Cable Extension: Unilateral version for imbalance correction
Reverse Grip Pushdown: Underhand grip to emphasize the medial head
Overhead Cable Extension: Facing away from the machine for long head emphasis

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
No Cable Machine: Use resistance bands anchored at a high point
Elbow Pain: Reduce weight and focus on controlled movement
Wrist Discomfort: Try a V-bar or EZ-bar attachment instead of rope
Shoulder Issues: Keep elbows tight to sides and avoid overhead variations
Beginner: Start with light weight and focus on mind-muscle connection
Want More Challenge: Add pause reps or slow eccentrics
